- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak or use 3-period moving average.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from high), model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias of 3–7% for next 2–3 periods.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to recent sentiment swings; smooth out 3-period moving average of forecast to reduce volatility.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; adjust forecast to match sentiment trend direction with 1–2% lag.
